items.title: Algorithmic Oversight: Caremark's Fiduciary Framework Applied to Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence now drives core corporate decision, such as loan approvals and hiring screens, yet corporate boards have largely treated its governance as a management-level policy questions rather than a fiduciary obligation. This paper argues that this framing is mistaken, using Delaware's Caremark doctrine, as refined by Marchand v. Barnhill, In re Boeing, and In re McDonald's. The relevant cases already impose an enforceable duty on boards to actively oversee mission algorithmic systems, and by applying Marchand's mission-critical standard, this paper demonstrates that AI performs core business functions that expose companies to anti-discrimination, consumer protection, and securities liability. The paper also identifies a structural problem that existing doctrine has not confronted: unlike the legible red flags at issue in Caremark, Boeing, and Clovis Oncology, AI systems generate outputs without human-readable explanations, allowing boards to receive clean compliance reports from systems that are producing unlawful outcomes. This "black box problem" requires reestablishing what good-faith oversight demands and when the underlying risk bypasses traditional reporting structures. Drawing on In re SolarWinds and the officer liability extension in McDonald's, this paper proposes a scalable framework for reasonable AI oversight, including board-level AI audit committees, a Chief AI Officer role with reporting duties to the General Counsel and CEO, mandatory governance disclosure, and a safe harbor for compliance. Ultimately, this paper challenges that the doctrinal tools to govern AI already exist within Delaware law, and all that remains is for boards to act before litigation forces the question.

items.title: Algorithmically Alone
items.abstract: Platform economies are reorganising the everyday conditions through which urban residents feel connected, isolated, or at home. Discussions of gig work typically begin with flexibility and income, overlooking how apps, ratings, incentives, and algorithmic decisions reshape the social setting of work itself. This chapter argues that urban loneliness should be understood not only as a private feeling but as an outcome shaped by how work, time, and urban space are organised. Drawing on social capital theory, economic sociology, urban studies, and research on algorithmic management, the chapter develops a conceptual framework explaining how platform design weakens some forms of social connection while enabling new forms of worker solidarity. The discussion considers how these dynamics intersect with gender, psychological strain, and migrant status. Cases from Uber, Ola, Urban Company, Indian delivery platforms, New York City, Seattle, the European Union, and India's social-security framework illustrate these dynamics in practice.

items.title: Alignment of bricolage practice: How supply chain managers mitigate risks through human–AI teaming
items.abstract: Background As organizations embed algorithmic agents in operations, alignment is presumed to make human–AI teams safer and more effective. Yet it leaves the orientation of alignment unexamined, that is, what humans and agents actually coordinate around. Objective Drawing on bricolage theory, this study distinguishes three orientations of alignment: tangible-resource, opportunity-oriented, and risk-oriented, then examines how each relates to collaborative fluency and to financial and inventory risk. Methods We analyzed 141 simulated supply-chain teams, each pairing a human manager with seven rule-based AI agents between 24 and 47 cycles. Behavioral logs were coded for alignment orientation, while collaborative fluency, risk behavior and outcomes were computed from logs by hierarchical regression. Results Tangible-resource alignment was associated with lower inventory redundancy and smaller drawdown. Risk-oriented alignment was associated with greater net-asset volatility and drawdown, associations that weakened once financing was controlled. Opportunity-oriented alignment showed no associations. No orientation explained collaborative fluency, and financing dominated financial risk. Conclusions Whether human–AI alignment reduces risk depends on its orientation. Tangible-resource alignment can buffer operational risk, but risk-oriented alignment may mark risk-taking rather than control it. Effective teaming depends less on more alignment than on aligning in right domain, with restraint in financing as the primary safeguard.

items.title: An End-to-End Workflow for Building Longitudinal Policy Measures From Government Web Sources Using Historical Reconstruction and LLM-Based Extraction
items.abstract: Background: Longitudinal policy research requires measures of what policy applied, when, and with what provisions, yet government sources are organized and preserved in ways that can make historical policy difficult to reconstruct. This study developed and evaluated an end-to-end workflow for constructing longitudinal policy measures from government web sources.Methods: The workflow was applied to NHS England’s Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS), a national policy specifying which primary-care workforce categories are eligible for reimbursement, from 2019/20 to 2026/27. It combined historical document recovery, variable specification, automated extraction against a human-coded reference standard, and longitudinal measure construction. Keyword, deterministic, and large language model (LLM) methods were compared across eight development and six later evaluation versions. Three simplified measurement strategies were compared with the author-verified longitudinal reference. Exploratory source recovery assessments were also conducted in Spain, France, and Australia.Results: Historical reconstruction identified 14 substantive document versions across eight policy years, including within-year changes in reimbursement eligibility, amounts, and conditions. Reimbursable primary-care workforce categories increased from 5 to 27, while the current NHS England landing page provided access to documents from only one policy year. On the six later evaluation versions, the LLM matched all scored reference-standard targets for eligibility status, effective dates, and reimbursement amounts, although eligibility conditions remained more difficult to extract. Simplified measurement strategies changed the reconstructed policy history. Using only the current specification could not recover historical eligibility, one specification per policy year assigned 96 eligible category-months (7.3%) too early, and keyword coding produced 138 category-month errors (10.5%).Conclusion: Valid longitudinal policy measurement requires historical reconstruction, explicit variable and dating rules, evaluation on later documents, and human verification. For health-politics research, this approach can support measures of changing governmental choices about eligibility, financing, conditions, and timing while distinguishing formal policy from implementation and outcomes.

items.title: An Idea to Explore: AI ‐Supported Digital Twin Laboratory for Risk‐Reduced and Immersive Biochemistry Education
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Biochemistry education faces persistent challenges in equipping students with the skills required to manage complex laboratory protocols, advanced instrumentation, and analytical procedures, particularly in high‐risk or resource‐intensive experimental settings. Traditional hands‐on training is constrained by limited access to equipment, safety concerns, and high operational costs, hindering institutions from providing realistic and scalable laboratory experiences. However, Digital Twin technology presents a transformative alternative. It creates simulations of real biochemical laboratories, providing immersive, scalable, and cost‐efficient environments unconstrained by physical limitations. This approach supports interactive, avatar‐mediated engagement that bridges conceptual knowledge with applied practice. In this study, we aimed to introduce BioDTLab, a custom Digital Twin framework for biochemistry education that integrates Virtual Reality, Internet of Things, robotics, data analytics, and an Artificial Intelligence (AI)‐driven Virtual Chat‐GPT Tutor. BioDTLab synchronizes physical and digital domains to provide high‐fidelity simulations of biochemical processes and instrumentation, while the AI‐driven Virtual Chat‐GPT Tutor evaluates student engagement, comprehension, and procedural accuracy. Our findings demonstrate that Digital Twin frameworks, such as BioDTLab, can redefine biochemistry education by making advanced experiential learning more accessible, safe, and scalable, while reducing reliance on costly physical resources. BioDTLab integrates immersive simulation, real‐time data synchronization, and AI‐driven feedback to provide a sustainable model for future science education that enhances conceptual understanding and practical competence. In addition, its adaptability makes it suitable for instructional models, such as the flipped classroom, where pre‐laboratory virtual practice can complement and enhance in‐person laboratory training.

items.title: An Integrated Community Engagement & Project Management System (Icepms) A Single-Window Digital Ecosystem for Research & Development in Higher Education Institutions in India
items.abstract: Abstract India's higher education system has never lacked policy mandates for community engagement. What it has consistently lacked is a working mechanism to connect community-identified problems with academic institutions positioned to address them. This paper proposes the Integrated Community Engagement & Project Management System (ICEPMS) — a single-window digital ecosystem that bridges this gap by linking community demand directly to higher education delivery. The paper develops a five-stakeholder conceptual model through systematic analysis of national policy documents, international frameworks, and established scholarship on community-based participatory research (CBPR) and service-learning. The proposed system enables citizens, Gram Panchayat members, NGOs, and journalists to report local problems digitally; allows administrators to convert those problems into credit-mapped academic topics; enables colleges and students to execute Community Engagement Projects; records performance transparently; and facilitates funding from CSR departments and government officers based on verifiable institutional performance. The paper discusses the role of artificial intelligence as a supportive accelerator within the system. ICEPMS aligns with the mandates of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the UGC Guidelines for Fostering Social Responsibility and Community Engagement in Higher Education Institutions in India 2.0 (2022), and institutional Community Engagement Project frameworks. By providing operational infrastructure for existing policy intent, the paper contributes a practical framework for community engagement in Indian higher education.

items.title: An Integrated Computer Vision and Machine Learning Framework for Sorghum Disease Severity Assessment and Yield Prediction
items.abstract: An Integrated Computer Vision and Machine Learning Framework for Sorghum Disease Severity Assessment and Yield Prediction presents a technology-driven approach for automated crop health monitoring and yield estimation in sorghum cultivation. The study integrates computer vision techniques and machine learning algorithms to identify and quantify disease severity from crop images and to predict potential yield based on relevant visual and agronomic characteristics. The framework aims to reduce the limitations of conventional manual disease assessment, which can be time-consuming and subject to human variability. Image processing and feature extraction techniques are employed to capture disease-related characteristics, while machine learning models support classification, severity estimation, and yield prediction. By combining disease assessment with yield forecasting, the proposed framework provides a comprehensive approach to precision agriculture and data-driven crop management. The work demonstrates the potential of artificial intelligence and computer vision to support timely decision-making, improve crop monitoring, and contribute to sustainable and efficient sorghum production.

items.title: An IoT-enabled multimodal AI system for classifying adolescent mental states using facial, motion, and postural data
items.abstract: This paper presents the design, development, and evaluation of a human-centric smart mental environment that integrates internet of things (IoT)-enabled sensors and artificial intelligence (AI) for the early detection of adolescent mental health indicators. Adolescent mental health disorders, including stress, anxiety, and depression, are increasingly prevalent yet remain underdiagnosed due to reliance on subjective self-reports and clinical interviews. Early detection is critical but hindered by symptom underreporting and the absence of continuous, objective monitoring tools suitable for real-world environments. To address this gap, the proposed system captures three complementary modalities: (1) facial expression features using a front-facing camera, (2) body motion and acceleration patterns using a wearable accelerometer and gyroscope, and (3) postural pressure distribution using an eight-element pressure array positioned along the thoracic and lumbar regions. Multimodal data are preprocessed using temporal-spatial filtering, followed by a cross-modal attention-based fusion mechanism that dynamically weights the most informative modality within each time window. A supervised learning classifier then predicts four mental states: normal, stress, anxiety, and depression. The system was evaluated using a dataset collected from 64 adolescents aged 14–18 under semi-natural, classroom-like conditions. The proposed attention-based multimodal framework achieved an overall classification accuracy of 89.2%, significantly outperforming unimodal baselines (facial-only: 77.8%, motion-only: 74.5%, posture-only: 71.3%) and simple concatenation fusion (83.5%). The attention mechanism improved the classification F1-score to 0.88 and demonstrated robustness under lighting and posture variations. Statistical analysis confirmed the superiority of the multimodal approach (p < 0.01). The system provides a non-invasive, scalable, and human-centric solution for continuous adolescent mental health monitoring, with strong potential for deployment in schools and community health programs.

items.title: Anal Dysplasia: From Pathogenesis to Risk-based Screening and Management
items.abstract: Anal dysplasia is the precursor of most anal squamous cell carcinomas and represents the central target of contemporary anal cancer prevention. Increasing recognition of high-risk populations, together with a better understanding of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated carcinogenesis and the results of the Anal Cancer/HSIL Outcomes Research (ANCHOR) trial, has shifted the focus from detecting disease to preventing cancer through the identification and treatment of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL). This chapter reviews the current concepts underlying anal dysplasia, including its epidemiology, natural history, risk factors, pathogenesis, histopathologic classification, diagnostic evaluation, and available therapeutic strategies. Particular emphasis is placed on the transition from the traditional anal intraepithelial neoplasia (AIN) classification to the Lower Anogenital Squamous Terminology (LAST) system, the pivotal role of high-resolution anoscopy with directed biopsy as the diagnostic reference standard, and the evidence supporting contemporary screening and treatment algorithms. Prevention is discussed as a continuum encompassing HPV vaccination, sexual health interventions, HIV prevention and treatment, early detection of HSIL, and long-term surveillance after therapy. Finally, the chapter highlights current challenges, including the need for standardized HRA training, development of centers of excellence, and international collaborative research to improve implementation, validate emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and precision risk prediction, and ultimately expand access to effective anal cancer prevention worldwide.

items.abstract: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is a crucial aspect of construction projects, particularly roof rehabilitation work, which carries a high risk of accidents. This study aims to identify hazards, analyze risk levels, and determine risk controls for the Kepulungan Community Health Center Roof Rehabilitation Project using the Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, and Risk Control (HIRARC) method. A qualitative descriptive approach was employed, involving observations, interviews, documentation reviews, and a literature study with 15 respondents. The results indicate that the dominant hazards were falls from heights (100%) with a risk score of 25 (extreme), being struck by falling materials (93.33%) with a score of 16 (high), slips/trips (86.67%) with a score of 12 (high), cuts/lacerations (80%) with a score of 6 (moderate), and electric shock (73.33%) with a score of 12 (high). Implemented controls included the use of Personal Protective Equipment (100%), safety briefings (93.33%), standard-compliant scaffolding (86.67%), safety officer supervision (86.67%), and OHS signage (80%). Workers' perceptions yielded an average score of 4.21 ("agree"), indicating that OHS risk management implementation has been effective. However, improvements in training, supervision of work at heights, and fall protection systems are still required to minimize workplace accidents..

items.abstract: This study aims to identify potential hazards, risk levels, and Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) control measures for the SDN II Sibon construction project in Pasrepan District. The study employs the Job Safety Analysis (JSA) method using a descriptive-qualitative approach, involving observations, interviews, documentation, and questionnaires administered to 16 workers. Risk assessment is conducted based on likelihood and severity parameters. The results indicate that workers' OHS knowledge ranges from reasonably good to high (62.5%–87.5%); however, the implementation of OHS measures is not yet optimal. The highest risks identified include heat exhaustion (81.25%), slipping (75%), and muscle pain (75%). Based on the JSA, three hazards were classified as extreme (scoring 20): soil collapse/stockpile collapse, excavation collapse, and falls from heights. Risk control measures implemented include engineering controls, administrative controls, and the use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)—specifically scaffolding and guardrails, shoring, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), toolbox meetings, OHS inspections, work permits, and task-specific PPE. Consistent implementation of these controls is expected to minimize accident risks and foster a safe, productive work environment.

items.title: Analisis Beban Kerja Instruktur Pelatihan Keselamatan Kerja Pertambangan Menggunakan Metode FTE
items.abstract: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is a fundamental pillar in the high-risk mining industry. Ensuring worker competence through mandatory safety training is a regulatory obligation under the Mining Safety Management System (SMKP). However, fluctuations in the number of training participants often lead to an imbalance in the workload of trainers, which can potentially reduce the quality of safety education. This study aims to evaluate the implementation of Training Need Analysis (TNA) and quantify the ideal requirement for safety trainers at PT Freeport Indonesia. The research design is descriptive quantitative. The research population includes all safety training programs under the Mining Safety Division. The sample taken consists of 21 mandatory training types within the Technical Support Division, with a total workload target of 10,872 training hours. The research variables include total training hours, classroom capacity, training frequency, and the effective working time of the trainers. Data collection was conducted through field observations and the recapitulation of the company's secondary ONA data. Data analysis utilizes mathematical calculations of the Full Time Equivalent (FTE) index. The results show that the mechanism for implementing TNA and training has normatively run systematically. However, the quantitative workload analysis reveals that the trainer's FTE index reaches 15.64. This figure indicates a significant workload excess (overload) within the safety training unit. It can be concluded that to complete the mandatory training targets within an optimal and safe six-month timeframe, a minimum availability of 16 trainers dedicated to the division is required.

items.abstract: The fishery processing and export industry is a key sector that contributes to the national economy, but it poses high occupational safety and health (OSH) risks due to the use of sharp equipment, manual handling of materials, exposure to low temperatures and chemicals, and forklift traffic. This study aims to identify hazards, assess risk levels, and develop control recommendations using the Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, and Risk Control (HIRARC) method based on the AS/NZS 4360:2004 standard and the Hierarchy of Control principle. The study employed a descriptive observational approach with a case study design in the fisheries processing and export industry in Indonesia. Data were collected through field observations and workplace safety inspections, then analyzed based on the likelihood and severity of risks. The study identified 23 potential hazards, consisting of 10 health hazards and 13 safety hazards. In the health hazard category, eight high-risk and two moderate-risk hazards were identified, while in the safety hazard category, there was one extreme-risk, seven high-risk, and five moderate-risk hazards. The highest risk stemmed from the intersection of forklift lanes with pedestrian walkways, which has the potential to cause fatal accidents. In addition, non-compliance issues were identified, such as expired fire extinguishers, the absence of safety signs at intersections, obstructed access to fire extinguishers, and inadequate ergonomic working conditions. The HIRARC method has proven effective in prioritizing risks as the basis for developing control measures. Control measures should prioritize extreme and high risks through engineering controls, administrative controls, routine inspections, and strengthening the occupational safety and health (OSH) culture to create a safer, healthier, and more productive work environment.

items.abstract: Construction projects are dynamic fields fraught with various risks that can affect productivity, performance, quality, and the project budget. This research aims to analyze the risks that emerged in the Mega Grup Indonesia Islamic School Ciamis Building Construction Project and determine appropriate handling strategies using the Failure Mode and Effect Analysis method. This research employs a quantitative approach with data collection techniques through field observation, interviews, and questionnaires involving 16 respondents directly involved in the project. The collected data were analyzed by calculating the severity, occurrence, and detection values for each identified risk. These values were then multiplied to obtain the risk priority number to determine risk handling priorities. The research results identified 17 potential risks. Three risks were categorized as high level: the influence of the rainy season and bad weather with an risk priority number of 74.4, work delays with an risk priority number of 61.8, and flooding with an risk priority number of 58. One risk fell into the medium category, namely workers' non-compliance with occupational health and safety regulations with an risk priority number of 40.2, and the other 13 risks were classified as low. As mitigation steps, material relocation can be implemented to address the influence of the rainy season and bad weather, adding labor to overcome work delays, cleaning drainage channels and utilizing water for flood risk, and providing personal protective equipment facilities and strict supervision to improve compliance with health and safety regulations for the risk of workers non-compliance with occupational health and safety rules.

items.title: ANALYSIS OF FACTORS AFFECTING THE OPERATIONAL EFFECTIVENESS OF AIRCRAFT CONTROL SYSTEMS
items.abstract: The article highlights the mismatch between existing design approaches and the conditions of modern combat operations, as reliability assessment is often conducted only for individual factors in isolation. Based on the system analysis, the authors identified and classified three main groups of influencing factors: natural (meteorological conditions, geophysical factors, and physical effects), anthropogenic (combat conditions, man-made interference, and the human factor), and technical (hardware, information-processing and algorithmic, and dynamic factors). Their components and the nature of each factor’s impact on the aircraft control system are described in detail. Based on the results of the analysis, three detailed structural-hierarchical diagrams of the influencing factors have been developed. The generalized structural-hierarchical framework allows for a comprehensive consideration of internal and external threats that arise throughout the entire aircraft lifecycle and directly affect combat employment effectiveness. The authors substantiate that the reliability and operational effectiveness of an aircraft control system must be considered as equivalent and interrelated characteristics. The created structural-hierarchical framework will serve as a foundation for the subsequent determination of the minimum necessary set of properties that modern and prospective aircraft control systems must possess.

items.title: Anchor-ECC: Local Integrity Checking for Watermarked LLM Outputs via Error-Correcting Codes
items.abstract: LLM watermarking has become an effective approach to distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text by embedding detectable patterns during generation. However, a small post-generation edit may change the meaning of the text without removing its overall watermark signal, creating a risk that the modified content is still attributed to the original model. We propose Anchor-ECC, which incorporates the error-correcting code (ECC) constraints and explicit boundary anchors into the watermark structure and pairs them with a dynamic-programming decoder to detect and localize post-generation edits. Across Qwen3-8B, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and OPT-125M, the approximate-hard setting achieves about 99.7% block-level true positive rate (TPR) with at most 7.6% false alarm rate (FAR) for edit detection under mixed insertions, deletions, and substitutions, while preserving the distinction between watermarked outputs and unwatermarked text. Additional quality experiments identify lower-perplexity configurations that retain strong edit-detection performance. Together, these results extend LLM watermarking from source identification to local integrity verification while supporting configurable trade-offs between detection reliability and generation quality.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Diagnostic Medical Imaging and Radiotherapy
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare, particularly in diagnostic imaging and radiotherapy. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of diagnostic medical imaging and radiotherapy has witnessed significant advancements, revolutionizing the healthcare landscape. This review delves into its diverse applications, exploring its potential to boost accuracy, streamline workflows, and improve patient outcomes. A systematic literature search identified relevant studies on AI's role in these domains. Articles covered topics like image analysis, pattern recognition, decision support, and treatment planning. AI algorithms, performance, and integration into clinical practice were critically evaluated. In diagnostic imaging, AI shines in modalities like MRI, CT, and PET. AI algorithms excel in image interpretation, aiding early detection, characterization, and staging of various diseases. Additionally, these tools show promise in predicting treatment response and personalizing treatment plans. Within radiotherapy, AI automates and improves treatment steps. Machine learning algorithms efficiently contour target volumes and organs at risk, facilitating optimal treatment planning. Real-time image guidance and AI-driven adaptive radiotherapy techniques enhance precision and safety during treatment delivery. Moreover, AI-based predictive models assist in assessing outcomes and optimizing therapeutic strategies, ultimately improving patient care. Despite the advancements, challenges like data privacy, standardization, and ethical considerations persist. This review paints a comprehensive picture of AI's current applications in diagnostic imaging and radiotherapy, highlighting its transformative impact on disease diagnosis and treatment planning. As AI evolves, its integration into clinical practice holds immense potential to revolutionize patient care, ushering in a new era of precision medicine.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Mathematics Teaching and Learning: Opportunities, Challenges and Future Prospects
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing mathematics education through personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, automated feedback, assessment support, and teacher assistance. AI-enabled systems can adapt tasks to learners’ needs, provide immediate feedback, generate practice questions, and help identify misconceptions. Recent reviews suggest that adaptive platforms, intelligent tutoring systems, and generative-AI tools can support engagement, self-paced learning, conceptual understanding, and mathematical problem-solving when used under effective teacher guidance.link.springer+1 However, AI is not a replacement for mathematics teachers. Concerns remain about inaccurate AI-generated solutions, student overdependence, privacy risks, unequal access to devices and internet connectivity, algorithmic bias, and limited teacher preparedness. Evidence also remains mixed, particularly because many studies are short-term and report limited standardized measures of learning impact. This paper reviews the opportunities and challenges of AI in mathematics teaching and learning and proposes a Human–AI Collaborative Framework for responsible, equitable, and pedagogically meaningful implementation.frontiersin+1

items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing mathematics education through personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, automated feedback, assessment support, and teacher assistance. AI-enabled systems can adapt tasks to learners’ needs, provide immediate feedback, generate practice questions, and help identify misconceptions. Recent reviews suggest that adaptive platforms, intelligent tutoring systems, and generative-AI tools can support engagement, self-paced learning, conceptual understanding, and mathematical problem-solving when used under effective teacher guidance.link.springer+1 However, AI is not a replacement for mathematics teachers. Concerns remain about inaccurate AI-generated solutions, student overdependence, privacy risks, unequal access to devices and internet connectivity, algorithmic bias, and limited teacher preparedness. Evidence also remains mixed, particularly because many studies are short-term and report limited standardized measures of learning impact. This paper reviews the opportunities and challenges of AI in mathematics teaching and learning and proposes a Human–AI Collaborative Framework for responsible, equitable, and pedagogically meaningful implementation.frontiersin+1

items.title: Application of Large Language Models and Natural Language Generation in Content Creation: A Retrieval-Augmented and Preference-Aligned Framework
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have substantially advanced natural language generation (NLG), but high-quality content creation remains constrained by hallucination, limited controllability, retrieval noise, domain shift, and computational cost. This study proposes Retrieval-Augmented and Preference-Aligned Generation (RAP-Gen), a unified framework that integrates retrieval-augmented generation, factual preference alignment, in-context learning, and denoising pre-training. The framework combines a dense semantic retriever with an encoder–decoder generator, introduces pairwise factual-preference supervision for controllable generation, aligns retrieval and generation distributions, and uses structured text corruption to improve robustness to incomplete or noisy inputs. Experiments are reported on summarization, long-form creative writing, and knowledge-intensive question answering using CNN/DailyMail, WritingPrompts, Natural Questions, and general language-modeling data. The reported results show that RAP-Gen improves ROUGE, BERTScore, perplexity, FactScore, and human-rated factuality relative to the baselines listed in the manuscript. Ablation results indicate that removing retrieval, preference alignment, or denoising degrades performance, supporting the complementary roles of external knowledge, preference signals, and robust pre-training. Additional analyses examine the number of retrieved documents, attention over retrieved evidence, robustness under input perturbation, model scaling, and in-context learning. Because the supplied material does not include raw predictions, code, repeated-run variance, annotator agreement statistics, or complete benchmark configurations, the numerical results are interpreted as reported experimental outcomes rather than independently reproducible evidence. The study contributes an integrated design for knowledge-grounded, preference-aware content generation and identifies evaluation and reproducibility requirements for future work.

items.title: Application of the ELMERI Observation Method for Occupational Health and Safety Performance Assessment in a Manufacturing Plant
items.abstract: Manufacturing workplaces involve hazards associated with machinery, material handling, worker practices, and environmental conditions. This study aimed to assess occupational health and safety conditions and identify priorities for improvement at a water fixture component manufacturing facility in Istanbul, Türkiye. A descriptive assessment was conducted using the ELMERI Observation Method across seven categories. A single researcher conducted observations three days per week from April to June 2021 and recorded 114 checklist-item ratings, comprising 74 correct and 40 incorrect classifications. Category-specific and overall safety indices were calculated from these counts. The overall index was 64.9%. Safety-related behavior had the highest category index (83.3%), followed by first aid and fire safety (71.4%), order and cleanliness (68.4%), and machine safety (66.7%). Lower indices were obtained for ergonomics (50.0%), industrial hygiene (44.4%), and floors and passageways (25.0%). The findings indicate that favorable ratings for observed worker practices coexisted with deficiencies in physical workplace conditions. Priorities included unobstructed passageways, machine guarding, ventilation, and ergonomic improvements. Unequal observation counts, potential observer bias, and the single-facility design limit interpretation and generalizability. The assessment identified practical priorities for the facility; the effectiveness of the proposed corrective actions requires follow-up evaluation.

items.title: Approach for Dual Probabilistic Linguistic Decision-Making Under Unknown Attribute Weights Based on Archimedean Power Muirhead Mean Operators
items.abstract: Dual probabilistic linguistic term sets (DPLTSs) provide a powerful tool for describing uncertain, hesitant, and bipolar linguistic assessments in complex decision-making settings. Current aggregation methods for dual probabilistic linguistic information still have drawbacks. They can hardly mitigate the interference brought by biased assessment values and fail to capture the correlations among arbitrary attributes. To address these limitations, this paper develops a new class of dual probabilistic linguistic Archimedean power Muirhead mean (DPLAPMM) operators for multipleattribute decision making (MADM). First, by combining the advantages of Archimedean triangular norms with the power Muirhead mean (PMM) operator, the DPLAPMM operator together with its weighted form are developed. The proposed operators can reduce the impact of unreasonable evaluation values while modeling the interrelationships among any number of attributes. Then, a dual probabilistic linguistic entropy is constructed to obtain objective attribute weights, which are combined with subjective weights to generate comprehensive attribute weights. Based on these results, a MADM method is established under a dual probabilistic linguistic environment. An illustrative case concerning industrial artificial intelligence (AI) project selection is used to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method, and comparative analyses show its flexibility and effectiveness over existing approaches.

items.title: ArchitectureIQ: On the Measure of Training Intuition
items.abstract: Top researchers have good intuition, but do language models have as good intuition about model training as top AI researchers? To measure model intuition of LLMs and humans, we introduce the ArchitectureIQ benchmark. Each question presents a synthetic dataset and several training recipes, and the test-taker is asked to predict the recipe yielding the best test metric. Overall, we find that LLMs' model intuition is good but has four limitations: (1) The intuition is imperfect, or even sub-human in some cases. Frontier models achieve around 76% accuracy (random choice 33%) vs best human researcher (66.0%), yet remain far from perfect. For architecture-only questions, best human achieves 65% while GPT-6 Astra only has 38%. (2) The intuition is empirical, not structured, supported by the fact that more CoT compute does not lead to substantial improvement. Unlike math, we still lack a "Science of AI" language that enables structured reasoning on AI. (3) The intuition is not maximally condensed, and can be further compressed into a knoledge base. Our constructed knowledge base with only 20 items yields large gains for weak models: GPT-4o equipped with the accumulated knowledge almost matches the performance of Claude Opus 5. (4) The intuition is insensitive to dataset properties, but the best model should in general depend on data properties. This suggests that data is the real "dark matter" in AI -- LLMs (so do human researchers) understand too little about data, even less than model architectures.

items.title: ARPE-IoT: Adaptive Recovery and Runtime Policy Enforcement for Resilient Cloud–Edge IoT Workflows
items.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence can improve Internet of Things (IoT) workflow resilience by reasoning over runtime context and generating recovery plans across devices, edge gateways, cloud services, and enterprise applications. However, autonomously completed recovery actions may still violate authorization, privacy, data-residency, actuator-safety, cost, or operational constraints. This paper proposes ARPE-IoT, an Adaptive Recovery and Policy Enforcement Framework for Agentic IoT Workflows. ARPE-IoT treats agent-generated recovery actions as proposals that must pass hard runtime policies before execution. Permissible actions are ranked using soft operational utility, executed under a bounded recovery budget, validated against workflow and physical-state conditions, audited, and escalated to humans when autonomous resolution is unsafe. We implemented a lightweight Python simulator with temperature and occupancy sensors, two edge gateways, two cloud services, an HVAC actuator, a policy engine, and a constrained recovery planner. Across 10,800 simulated executions covering normal operation and eight injected failure classes, ARPE-IoT achieved a 100% safe handling rate, consisting of 82.2% autonomous resolution and 17.8% controlled safe-state escalation. It reduced policy violations from 22.2% for unconstrained agents and 33.3% for rule-based recovery to 0% in the evaluated scenarios, with 47.7 ms mean latency.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Changing Patterns of Human Social Interaction
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into daily life is fundamentally reshaping the landscape of human social interaction and communication patterns. AI-powered tools, from sophisticated chatbots and virtual assistants to complex social media algorithms, are increasingly mediating, augmenting, and, in some cases, replacing human-to-human communication. This paper explores the transformative impact of AI on how people connect, express emotions, and form relationships. We examine the dual nature of this shift, highlighting the benefits of enhanced efficiency, accessibility, and personalization, while also scrutinizing the profound risks, including the potential for social isolation, the erosion of authentic connection, the creation of algorithmic echo chambers, and ethical challenges such as bias and lack of transparency. Ultimately, the paper argues that navigating the future of social interaction requires a critical balance between embracing AI's capabilities and prioritizing the core human values of empathy, connection, and ethical accountability.

items.title: Artificial intelligence adoption and organizational efficiency: the mediating role of organizational learning capability and moderating role of digital literacy
items.abstract: Introduction Strategic and organizational solutions are becoming essential due to the global demand for digital transformation, sustained operational efficiency, and the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. This study examines the influence of artificial intelligence adoption on organizational efficiency, with digital literacy as a boundary condition and organizational learning capability serving as a mediator. Methods The study utilized a quantitative cross-sectional survey-based design. A multistage sampling technique was used to collect data from employees working in the Ghanaian banking sector. Data collected from 388 employees from the banks were utilized in an empirical study employing structural equation modeling. Both direct and indirect relationships were assessed. Results The findings revealed that the level of artificial intelligence adoption has a significant and positive influence on both organizational efficiency and organizational learning capability. The results further showed that organizational learning capability has a significant and positive influence on organizational efficiency and partially mediates the relationship between artificial intelligence adoption and organizational efficiency. Additionally, the results revealed that digital literacy moderates the relationships between artificial intelligence adoption and organizational efficiency, as well as the relationships between organizational learning capability and organizational efficiency. Conclusion This study introduces a novel theoretical framework that connects the hitherto overlooked linkages between artificial intelligence adoption, organizational learning capability, digital literacy, and organizational efficiency within the banking sector of an emerging economy. By integrating these constructs into a unified model, the study clarifies the mechanisms and boundary conditions through which AI adoption translates into organizational efficiency, thereby extending the Resource-Based View in an emerging-market context.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and auditing: Legal and ethical implications for assurance providers
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing audit practice by expanding analytical coverage, automating routine procedures, and supporting more continuous risk assessment. These benefits, however, also raise questions about accountability, explainability, professional judgment, data protection, and legal responsibility. This study examines whether AI auditability and oversight design shape assurance professionals’ perceptions of ethical risk, legal exposure, and audit quality in Ghana. Using a quantitative design, the study combines a cross-sectional survey of 180 assurance professionals with a between-subjects vignette experiment. AI auditability was assessed in terms of data traceability, model documentation, explainability, governance controls, role clarity, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) procedures. The experiment compared manual-only auditing, AI-only auditing, and AI-assisted auditing with HITL oversight. AI auditability was negatively associated with perceived ethical risk (β = −0.456, p < .001) and positively associated with perceived audit quality (β = 0.424, p < .001). Perceived ethical risk was positively associated with perceived legal exposure (β = 0.536, p < .001) and negatively associated with perceived audit quality (β = −0.268, p < .001). Although AI auditability was negatively correlated with perceived legal exposure, its direct regression effect was not statistically significant after ethical risk was controlled (β = −0.092, p = .392). The experiment showed that AI-only oversight was associated with higher perceptions of ethical and legal risk than AI-assisted auditing with HITL oversight. Because the study measures professional perceptions rather than observed legal events or realized audit outcomes, the findings should be interpreted as evidence about perceived risk and quality. items.title: Artificial Intelligence And future of Library and Information Services: A conceptual Perspective
items.abstract: Abstract In the era of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the field of Library and Information Science is evolving rapidly with the introduction of new paradigms in information management, information discovery, and service delivery. This is a conceptual paper that analyses the role of AI and its future implications on the library and information services. It examines key AI technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, chatbots, robotics, AI-powered discovery services, personalized information services and generative AI, and explores how these are being used in modern libraries. This paper emphasises the benefits of these technologies in information retrieval, automating repetitive library functions, delivering personalized services to users, facilitating research activities, and engaging users. It also looks at how technology is evolving like smart libraries and AI-driven information services. Meanwhile, the paper covers important challenges that must be addressed in the context of the adoption of AI, such as privacy, data security, algorithmic bias, misinformation, copyright, ethical issues, technological costs, and technical skills. The evolving nature of the role of LIS professionals and the skills needed to collaborate with emerging AI technologies are given special attention. The paper proposes that AI is not the end of librarians but an enabler and a supportive tool for librarians. By combining AI with professional knowledge, ethical considerations, and human-centred services, libraries can become smarter, more efficient, user-friendly, and responsive to user needs. The study highlights the need for responsible use of AI, ongoing professional growth, and collaboration between technology and human skills to shape the future of library services. items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Global Business Operations: Evidence from Amazon and Implications for Responsible Enterprise Adoption
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an established part of how organizations run their operations, from customer interaction and demand forecasting to logistics, marketing, and knowledge work. This paper examines what that means for global business operations through a documentary case study of Amazon. The study does not collect primary data or measure Amazon's performance independently. It analyzes publicly available sources: Amazon's corporate publications and regulatory filings, reports from international institutions, and peer-reviewed research. The paper keeps a clear line between what Amazon reports having deployed and what independent evidence shows about outcomes. The paper finds that AI can support productivity, personalization, forecasting, automation, and human decision support, but that the effects are neither automatic nor uniform. Drawing on independent studies, it notes that productivity gains can be substantial for some workers, particularly less-experienced ones, while AI can reduce performance on tasks outside its effective capability range. Amazon illustrates how AI can be integrated across a value chain, including recommendations, fulfilment and robotics, demand forecasting, and generative-AI services. The case also shows why adoption needs governance, workforce development, data management, risk assessment, and human oversight. The paper concludes with an eight-step framework for responsible enterprise AI adoption. It starts from a defined business problem, evaluates AI at the level of individual tasks, and draws on the NIST AI Risk Management Framework for risk management. It argues that the value of AI depends less on the technology itself than on organizational readiness and the quality of human-AI collaboration.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Higher Education under NEP 2020: A Competency-Based Framework for Achieving Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract AI and ML are rapidly changing higher education by redefining teaching, learning, research, evaluation, and institutional governance. India's National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 envisions a transdisciplinary, technology-enabled, learner-centric, and innovation-driven education system that produces globally competent graduates who can contribute to Viksit Bharat 2047. Despite rising acceptance of AI-based educational technology, equitable access, faculty preparedness, ethical governance, digital infrastructure, and curriculum revision for future workforce needs remain problems. This study critically investigates how AI and ML might improve the quality, accessibility, inclusivity, and effectiveness of higher education in India within NEP 2020. It examines the transformative potential of AI-enabled adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring, predictive learning analytics, automated assessment, academic administration, and research support, using a doctrinal and analytical research methodology grounded in policy documents, government reports, and contemporary academic literature. It also highlights algorithmic unfairness, data privacy, cybersecurity, digital inequality, academic integrity, and ethical issues in the implementation of generative AI. The Competency-Based AI Integration Framework (AI-HE 2047 Framework) integrates digital literacy, critical thinking, interdisciplinary learning, research and innovation, ethical AI governance, and lifelong learning competencies to align AI adoption with the goals of NEP 2020. The methodology helps higher education institutions produce AI-ready graduates for an innovation-driven knowledge economy. The study found that responsible integration of AI and ML, supported by policy reforms, faculty capacity building, institutional readiness, and ethical governance mechanisms, can improve educational quality, employability, research excellence, and India's transition to a knowledge-powered economy under Viksit Bharat 2047.
